papers.title_en: Observer-Based Control for Multi-Agent Systems under Communication-Task Graph Mismatch and Directed Switching Topologies
papers.authors: Tommaso Zaccherini, Siyuan Liu, Dimos V. Dimarogonas
papers.evidence: 面向多智能体协调的分布式估计与控制
papers.tldr: 针对异构多智能体在通信图与任务图不匹配及有向切换拓扑下的分散估计与控制问题，提出基于k-hop预设性能状态观测器（k-hop PPSO）的方法。各智能体仅用1-hop邻居信息估计k跳内状态，并设计预设性能漏斗及驻留时间下界以应对拓扑切换。理论分析表明，在闭环对估计误差满足一致集合ISS时，用估计替代非局部状态可使系统收敛到期望集邻域，且邻域可任意小。仿真验证了有向切换拓扑下任务协调的有效性。
papers.abstract_en: This paper addresses decentralized estimation and control of heterogeneous multi-agent systems communicating over directed switching topologies. The objective is to satisfy cooperative tasks that require coordination among agents according to a time-invariant task graph. To address the potential mismatch between the communication and task graphs, each agent is equipped with a k-hop Prescribed Performance State Observer (k-hop PPSO) to estimate the states of agents up to k communication hops away using only information exchanged with its 1-hop neighbors. A novel prescribed performance funnel construction is developed to account for the switching communication topology, and a sufficient lower bound on the dwell-time is derived to guarantee the prescribed performance specifications under topology variations. Further analysis shows that, if the desired control objective is achieved with exact knowledge of the required nonlocal states and the resulting closed-loop system is uniformly set-ISS with respect to the state estimation error, then replacing these states with their estimates guarantees convergence to a neighborhood of the desired set. The size of this neighborhood can be made arbitrarily small by appropriately selecting the observer performance bounds. A simulation study demonstrates task satisfaction under directed switching topologies.

papers.title_en: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
papers.authors: Jad Yammine, Malek Wahidi, Abrar Anwar, Yan Chang, Mihir Acharya, Anthony Rizk
papers.evidence: 仓储机器人车队的共享时空语义记忆
papers.tldr: 仓库机器人车队视频若保存为可复用语义记忆，会带来高计算、通信与存储开销。IndustrialReMEmbR在Jetson端用Cosmos-Embed1、Cosmos3-Edge与Wan2.2 VAE提取检索嵌入、视觉token和重建潜变量，不上传原始帧且按需描述。系统拆分Cosmos3-Edge，视觉编码器留机器人、语言解码器放服务器，Nemotron按内容、位置和时间检索并缓存token解码。450次测试解码均复现未拆分模型输出，支持PII抽象与GDPR合规。
papers.abstract_en: Warehouse robot fleets continuously observe operational conditions, but preserving these observations as reusable semantic memory incurs substantial computation, communication, and storage costs. For example, explaining recurring aisle blockages can require reviewing video from multiple robots across several shifts. We present IndustrialRemembr, a shared spatiotemporal memory system that extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR to robot fleets and reduces server-side computation by generating scene descriptions only on demand. On each robot, an NVIDIA Jetson encodes video clips into retrieval embeddings with Cosmos-Embed1, vision tokens with Cosmos3-Edge, and reconstruction latents with the Wan2.2 VAE, without uploading raw camera frames. The encoding models are re-used to detect people in image patches, zeroing them out to support PII abstraction for GDPR-compliant deployments. We split Cosmos3-Edge at its vision-language boundary, placing the vision encoder on the robot and the language decoder on an on-premises server. A Nemotron agent retrieves memories by content, position, and time and queries the decoder using cached vision tokens. This design eliminates caption generation at write time, while cached-token decoding reproduces the unsplit model's output in all 450 tested decodes.

papers.title_en: Discovery-Probability Graph Planning for Embodied Agents in Tasks with Hidden Cooperation Requirements
papers.authors: Zihuang Cai, Changjian Chen, Zhuo Tang, Chang Tang, Kenli Li
papers.evidence: 面向隐藏协作需求的具身多智能体图规划协作方法
papers.tldr: 具身智能体常被假定合作任务已知，但现实中合作需求往往要在观察和交互目标后才显现。为此作者提出HiddenCoop基准与Discovery-Probability Graph Planning（DPGP）方法，用发现概率图编码任务目标数量与位置分布并规划最小期望成本动作。实验在C-WAH和TDW-MAT上分别达到99.3%和58.3%成功率，优于基线并降低执行时间与LLM token消耗。该工作为隐藏合作需求下的具身多智能体规划提供了评测与高效方案。
papers.abstract_en: Embodied agents are increasingly capable of perceiving, planning, and acting autonomously in dynamic environments, demonstrating strong performance on complex cooperative tasks. Recent advances typically assume that cooperative tasks are known in advance. In real-world applications, however, hidden-cooperation tasks are more common: the need for cooperation only becomes apparent after an agent observes and interacts with task-related targets. In this paper, we first present HiddenCoop, a benchmark for effectively evaluating agent cooperation in hidden-cooperation tasks. We further propose Discovery-Probability Graph Planning (DPGP), a method for enabling effective agent cooperation in such tasks. At the core of DPGP is a discovery-probability graph that encodes the probability distribution over the number and locations of task-related targets, facilitating effective and efficient information exchange among agents. A search algorithm is then used to derive action plans that minimize expected costs. Experiments show that DPGP achieves cooperative-task success rates of 99.3% on C-WAH and 58.3% on TDW-MAT, surpassing all compared baselines, while also reducing overall embodied execution time and substantially lowering LLM token usage. Our code is available at https://github.com/hnu-vis/DPGP.

papers.title_en: Robot-Task Suitability in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Task Allocation
papers.evidence: 基于机器人—任务适配度估计的异构多机器人任务分配
papers.tldr: 异构多机器人任务分配依赖对机器人—任务适配度的估计，但适配度定义方式差异巨大。本文系统比较十种确定性方法与两种基于大语言模型的变体，涵盖规则、相似度、需求导向、模糊与语义等思路。在统一机器人与任务画像下，考察打分排序、可行性判定与最优机器人选择，并分析团队构成、规模、空间上下文、能力不确定性与任务表示的影响。结果显示方法间常出现分歧，通用相似度可能违背单侧需求满足性质，LLM评分还引入随机性与语言敏感性。
papers.abstract_en: Heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation depends on estimates of how suitable individual robots are for candidate tasks, yet suitability can be defined in substantially different ways. We compare ten deterministic methods and two LLM-based variants spanning rule-based, similarity-based, requirement-oriented, fuzzy, and semantic approaches. Using common robot and task profiles, we compare how the methods score and rank candidate robots, identify feasibility, and select a top robot, while examining how these outcomes change with team composition, scale, spatial context, capability uncertainty, and task representation. The methods frequently disagree despite operating on identical scenarios. Generic similarity measures can violate properties expected under a one-sided requirement-satisfaction interpretation of suitability, while LLM-based scoring introduces additional stochastic and linguistic sensitivity. These results show that robot--task suitability should be treated as an explicit modeling choice whose assumptions, robustness, and decision-level consequences should be considered before allocation.

papers.title_en: Safe Multi-Robot Collaboration With Uniform Exclusion Using Trust
papers.authors: Thomas Kaminsky, Áron Vékássy, Hammad Izhar, Angelia Nedić, Stephanie Gil
papers.evidence: 基于可信通信链路的安全多机器人协作
papers.tldr: 机器人集群依赖有向时变局部通信，部分链路可能被劫持并注入恶意数据。本文提出通信包装器Safe Wrapper，用Safe Anytime-Valid Inference检验各机器人异常检测器输出的信任值流，为状态更新筛选可信链路，仅要求检测器优于随机。理论上可高概率在所有时刻统一排除全部受损链路，同时快速信任合法链路。硬件在3台LoCoBots和8台GoPiGos上验证神经隐式建图与朝向共识，仿真显示可扩展至数百机器人。
papers.abstract_en: Robot swarms coordinate through directed, time-varying local communication links, some of which may be compromised to allow the transmission of arbitrary malicious data. We provide an algorithm that acts as a wrapper around robot communication---when a robot seeks to update its state using data from some incoming links, our wrapper provides a subset of trusted links whose data can be safely incorporated. It selects these links by testing a stream of trust values---data collected from an anomaly detector on each robot---using Safe Anytime-Valid Inference. We require only that the detector be better than chance. This wrapper ensures safe and performant autonomy by providing two powerful statistical guarantees: it uniformly excludes all compromised links for all time with high user-chosen probability, but nevertheless quickly learns to trust legitimate links. Both guarantees are vital to secure generic tasks, but no previous work provides them simultaneously without restrictive assumptions on connectivity structure or the number of compromised links that are not guaranteed in practice. We study our Safe Wrapper's performance in hardware for two contrasting tasks---neural implicit mapping and heading consensus---deploying on 3 LoCoBots and 8 GoPiGos, respectively. We provide simulations using trust values sampled from hardware to validate that our approach scales well to swarms of hundreds of robots.
